assertion.prompt: SARS-CoV-2 infection has been associated with both incident type 1 and type 2 diabetes, yet the mechanistic pathways and patient risk factors that predispose to one versus the other remain unclear. Do viral and/or host immune and metabolic pathways distinguish type 1 (autoimmune beta-cell destruction) from type 2 (insulin resistance + relative beta-cell inadequacy) post-COVID trajectories?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#SARS-CoV-2 Spike-Mediated Entry via ACE2 and TMPRSS2
assertion.rationale: Meta-analyses and prospective cohorts report increased incidence of both type 1 diabetes (especially in children with new-onset DKA above baseline) and type 2 diabetes (particularly in hospitalized and older adults). The role of SARS-CoV-2 as a direct trigger of autoimmunity, a driver of insulin resistance through persistent inflammation, or an unmasker of pre-existing glucose intolerance is not yet resolved. Mechanistic and genetic factors that predict which type develops are largely unknown.

selected_evidence.snippet: Soon, additional studies began to identify similar increases in new-onset type 2 diabetes [17].

assertion.prompt: Mac1-directed therapy works by lifting viral suppression of host ADP-ribosylation, so its benefit is predicted to depend on the patient's own interferon competence. Does a Mac1 inhibitor retain efficacy in the roughly one in five patients with critical COVID-19 who carry anti-type-I interferon autoantibodies or an inborn error of type I interferon immunity, and should interferon autoantibody status therefore be a companion diagnostic rather than an exclusion?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#RNA Virus-Induced Interferon and PARP Activation
assertion.rationale:
Every published Mac1 inhibitor whose mechanism has been dissected acts through immune restoration rather than through direct antiviral blockade, and in both compound series the cellular antiviral effect is explicitly interferon dependent. That makes host interferon competence a gate on the entire therapeutic strategy, and the gate is not hypothetical: inborn errors of type I interferon immunity account for 1 to 5 percent of unvaccinated patients with critical pneumonia and anti-interferon autoantibodies for another 15 to 20 percent, so the patients most likely to need a novel antiviral are enriched for the defect that would blunt it.
The gap is that this has never been tested. No Mac1 inhibitor has entered a clinical trial, so no cohort stratified by interferon autoantibody status or by interferon-stimulated gene score exists, and the preclinical interferon dependence has only been shown by adding or withholding interferon gamma in culture, not by comparing hosts that differ in endogenous type I interferon capacity. Resolving it needs either an animal model with defined type I interferon pathway loss treated with an active-site Mac1 inhibitor, or prospective collection of anti-interferon autoantibody status in any future trial. The answer bears directly on the Mac1 pivot hypothesis's claim of broad activity, because the limitation applies equally to active-site, allosteric, and degradation-based approaches.

assertion.prompt: What distinguishes acute hyperglycemia during COVID-19 hospitalization (stress-hyperglycemia) from persistent de novo diabetes development post-COVID? Do the pathways driving acute metabolic decompensation during infection differ mechanistically from those driving long-term beta-cell loss or insulin resistance post-infection?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#SARS-CoV-2 Spike-Mediated Entry via ACE2 and TMPRSS2
assertion.rationale: COVID-19 hospitalized patients frequently develop hyperglycemia (~50%), but the majority resolve it post-discharge. However, population cohort studies (OpenSAFELY, N3C) and registry data report incident diabetes cases years post-infection. The mechanism(s) linking acute infection-driven hyperglycemia to persistent diabetes risk is not clear: stress-hyperglycemia may unmask pre-existing insulin resistance that progresses to type 2 diabetes, acute direct infection of beta cells may cause lasting damage, or unresolved post-viral inflammation may sustain pathways months/years later. A prospective multi-timepoint mechanistic study is needed.

selected_evidence.snippet: stress- and treatment-induced hyperglycaemia is common in critical illness, occurring in approximately 50% of affected individuals. While often transient, these effects may unmask persistent metabolic dysfunction in individuals at risk of type 2 diabetes [36, 37].

assertion.prompt: Does SARS-CoV-2 directly infect and damage pancreatic beta cells during acute COVID-19, or is acute hyperglycemia driven predominantly by systemic inflammation, HPA-axis stress, and metabolic dysregulation in peripheral insulin-sensitive tissues?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#SARS-CoV-2 Spike-Mediated Entry via ACE2 and TMPRSS2
assertion.rationale: Post-acute SARS-CoV-2 infection has been associated with new-onset diabetes, raising the mechanistic question of direct viral pancreatic tropism vs. systemic inflammation as the driver. A comprehensive post-pandemic review (Said et al. 2026, Diabetologia) identifies conflicting evidence on whether SARS-CoV-2 directly infects pancreatic beta cells during acute infection, or whether acute hyperglycemia and persistent metabolic dysfunction post-COVID result from HPA-axis stress, pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF, IL-6, IL-1beta), and reduced peripheral insulin sensitivity. This distinction is mechanistically consequential: direct beta-cell tropism could produce permanent damage and predict Type 1-like post-COVID diabetes, whereas inflammation-mediated dysfunction would predict reversible Type 2 hyperglycemia. Resolution of this branch informs the mechanistic link to post-COVID diabetes development modeled in Long_COVID entry.

selected_evidence.snippet: We summarise proposed pathophysiological mechanisms, including the effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection in the pancreas and on peripheral insulin-sensitive tissues. We review key meta-analyses assessing the association between COVID-19 and incident type 1 and type 2 diabetes and highlight strengths and weaknesses of the epidemiologic studies

assertion.prompt: Mac1-directed therapy works by lifting viral suppression of host ADP-ribosylation, so its benefit is predicted to depend on the patient's own interferon competence. Does a Mac1 inhibitor retain efficacy in the roughly one in five patients with critical COVID-19 who carry anti-type-I interferon autoantibodies or an inborn error of type I interferon immunity, and should interferon autoantibody status therefore be a companion diagnostic rather than an exclusion?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#RNA Virus-Induced Interferon and PARP Activation
assertion.rationale:
Every published Mac1 inhibitor whose mechanism has been dissected acts through immune restoration rather than through direct antiviral blockade, and in both compound series the cellular antiviral effect is explicitly interferon dependent. That makes host interferon competence a gate on the entire therapeutic strategy, and the gate is not hypothetical: inborn errors of type I interferon immunity account for 1 to 5 percent of unvaccinated patients with critical pneumonia and anti-interferon autoantibodies for another 15 to 20 percent, so the patients most likely to need a novel antiviral are enriched for the defect that would blunt it.
The gap is that this has never been tested. No Mac1 inhibitor has entered a clinical trial, so no cohort stratified by interferon autoantibody status or by interferon-stimulated gene score exists, and the preclinical interferon dependence has only been shown by adding or withholding interferon gamma in culture, not by comparing hosts that differ in endogenous type I interferon capacity. Resolving it needs either an animal model with defined type I interferon pathway loss treated with an active-site Mac1 inhibitor, or prospective collection of anti-interferon autoantibody status in any future trial. The answer bears directly on the Mac1 pivot hypothesis's claim of broad activity, because the limitation applies equally to active-site, allosteric, and degradation-based approaches.

selected_evidence.snippet: Standard cellular models indicate that AVI-4206 has high target engagement and can weakly inhibit viral replication in a gamma interferon- and Mac1 catalytic activity-dependent manner.

assertion.prompt: Why do CNS, gastrointestinal and lymphoid compartments transform preferentially in CMMRD when mismatch repair is absent from every tissue?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Constitutional Microsatellite Instability and Mutator Phenotype
assertion.rationale: Constitutional instability is systemic, yet the tumour spectrum is not. Constitutional instability scores differ by tissue (gastrointestinal > blood > brain) and rise with age within an individual, so the tissue-specific transformation risk is not simply a function of measured instability. The determinants - proliferative index of the stem compartment, tissue-specific dependence on MMR versus backup pathways, immune surveillance, or the tissue-specific probability of acquiring the somatic POLE/POLD1 hit - have not been disentangled. Getting this right would sharpen surveillance intervals, which are currently uniform rather than risk-weighted by tissue.

proposed_experiments.name: Clone-resolved mutation burden across matched normal tissues in CMMRD
proposed_experiments.description: Measure somatic mutation burden and microsatellite indel load at single-cell or clone-resolved depth in matched normal brain, intestinal crypt and haematopoietic compartments from the same CMMRD individual, and test whether the compartment with the highest measured instability is the compartment that transforms first.

proposed_experiments.name: Longitudinal constitutional-instability scoring against organ of first cancer
proposed_experiments.description: Score constitutional genomic instability serially in blood and, where available, gastrointestinal tissue from a prospective CMMRD surveillance cohort, and test whether the instability trajectory predicts the organ and timing of the first cancer well enough to justify tissue-weighted rather than uniform surveillance intervals.

selected_evidence.snippet: In normal cells, MMRDness scores differed between tissues (GI > blood > brain), increased over time in the same individual, and revealed genotype-phenotype associations within the mismatch repair genes.

assertion.prompt: How much residual mismatch repair activity is compatible with an adult-onset, Lynch-like phenotype, and where does the CMMRD/Lynch management boundary fall for biallelic carriers of hypomorphic variants?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Biallelic Germline Mismatch Repair Gene Inactivation
assertion.rationale: Late-onset CMMRD is currently recognised case by case, after constitutional MSI testing contradicts an assumed Lynch diagnosis. There is no calibrated relationship between residual repair activity and age at first cancer, so a biallelic carrier of two leaky variants cannot be assigned to a surveillance schedule on genotype. The two schedules differ substantially (annual brain MRI and gastrointestinal endoscopy from early childhood in CMMRD; adult gastrointestinal and gynaecological surveillance in Lynch), so the cost of guessing is high in both directions.

proposed_experiments.name: Calibration of residual mismatch repair activity against age at first cancer
proposed_experiments.description: Assay residual mismatch repair activity quantitatively across a series of candidate hypomorphic MMR variants (leaky splice and missense alleles) and correlate the measured activity with constitutional instability score and age at first cancer, to establish whether residual activity predicts the CMMRD-versus-Lynch management boundary.

proposed_experiments.name: Constitutional MSI screening of adults with biallelic MMR variants of uncertain significance
proposed_experiments.description: Systematically apply constitutional microsatellite instability testing to adult patients carrying biallelic or compound-heterozygous MMR variants of uncertain significance who are currently managed as Lynch syndrome, to estimate how often late-onset CMMRD is being missed.

selected_evidence.snippet: Individualised management of mono- and bi-allelic carriers of hypomorphic MMR variants is needed until we better characterise the associated phenotypes.

assertion.prompt: Does the complex II-dependent oxidative mechanism established in rat microglial cultures hold in human basal ganglia, where the affected cell populations, manganese concentrations, and exposure durations all differ?
attaches_to: pathophysiology#Microglial Complex II-Dependent Reactive Oxygen Species Production
assertion.rationale: The evidence assigning the oxidative lesion of manganese to respiratory complex II rather than complex I is strong but comes from acute exposure of isolated rat microglia to low micromolar Mn(2+). Human manganism arises from chronic exposure over years, and the node sits in a chain whose downstream effector is a pallidal circuit lesion rather than a microglial one. Three things are therefore open: whether complex II dependence is a property of microglia specifically or of manganese-exposed cells generally; whether the same selectivity holds at the far lower concentrations reached over chronic human exposure; and how much of the human pallidal injury this route accounts for. The mismatch matters for curation because it is the sole basis for this entry declining to conform to the parkinsonism module's complex I node, so if the complex II selectivity turned out to be a feature of the acute rodent preparation, that decision would need revisiting.

selected_evidence.snippet: Mn(2+) was capable of inducing significant H2O2 production in the mitochondrial but not the cytosolic or nuclear fraction prepared from microglia

assertion.prompt: Does manganism produce tremor, and if so what kind?
assertion.rationale: The cached reviews do not agree. One describes a rapid postural tremor among the motor impairments; a second says resting tremor specifically is not a distinguishing feature, which is consistent with the first; and a third states flatly that patients with manganism have no tremor at all. The disagreement is not obviously about the same thing - a source denying "tremor" may mean the resting tremor of Parkinson disease, which the other sources also deny - but none of them says so, and this entry does not have the evidence to decide it. The phenotype is curated with the postural characterisation and carries the denial as a REFUTE. It matters because tremor quality is one of the features the Parkinson disease differential rests on.

selected_evidence.snippet: This syndrome is characterized by bradykinesia, rigidity, and tremor

assertion.prompt: Manganese induces alpha-synuclein aggregation in exposed primates, and human manganese overload is characterised by negative alpha-synuclein immunostaining. Does the primate finding describe anything that happens in human manganism?
assertion.rationale: The mismatch is sharp rather than gradual. In Mn-exposed cynomolgus macaques, alpha-synuclein-positive neurons and glia appear in frontal cortex grey and white matter. In humans with pallidal manganese accumulation measured directly at autopsy, alpha-synuclein immunostaining was negative in all but one case, and the defining neuropathology of manganism is the absence of Lewy bodies. Both cannot be generalised. Possible reconciliations: the primate aggregates are a different species of assembly from Lewy pathology; the cortical location differs from the pallidal region sampled in the human series; or the primate exposure regimen produces something the human occupational one does not. This matters because alpha-synuclein is the bridge people use to argue that manganese exposure causes Parkinson disease, and the human pathology is the main evidence against that.

selected_evidence.snippet: Neuropathology revealed mild to moderate Alzheimer type II gliosis in the liver failure groups and negative alpha-synuclein and tau immunostaining except for one case

assertion.prompt: What is the prevalence of parkinsonism among manganese-exposed workers, and can the widely cited welder figures be used for it?
assertion.rationale: The most-cited occupational prevalence estimates come from a screen of 1,423 Alabama welders who were referred for medical-legal evaluation for Parkinson disease. That is a population selected for having, or claiming, the outcome being measured, so the resulting rate cannot be read as an occupational prevalence, and this entry records no prevalence figure rather than launder one. The exposure-response relationship from the trade-union longitudinal cohort is a different and sounder claim, and is the one the entry carries.

selected_evidence.snippet: The authors screened 1,423 welders from Alabama who were referred for medical-legal evaluation for Parkinson disease (PD).

assertion.prompt: Is the dopaminergic system in manganism untouched, or functionally impaired without degenerating?
assertion.rationale: The textbook account is that manganism spares the nigrostriatal dopaminergic neurons, and the neuropathology supports it: substantia nigra pars compacta preserved, no Lewy bodies. But asymptomatic welders show measurably reduced FDOPA uptake, and Mn-exposed primates show marked inhibition of dopamine release with terminals intact. These are not contradictory once function and structure are kept apart - the terminals are there and underperforming - but the entry should not be read as claiming the dopaminergic system is unaffected. The FDOPA pattern is also the discriminating detail: reduced, but caudate-first, which is the reverse of the posterior-putamen-first pattern of idiopathic Parkinson disease.

selected_evidence.snippet: This uptake pattern was anatomically reversed from the pattern found in subjects with IPD.

assertion.prompt: Does manganism stabilise, improve, or continue to progress after exposure stops?
assertion.rationale: Removal from exposure is the main intervention, and what it achieves is not settled. Reviews describe symptoms persisting after the source is eliminated, and at least one series describes progression through the first decade after cessation before plateauing. The methcathinone series found deficits that did not resolve. Against that, blood manganese falls and MRI signal fades, so the biomarkers improve while the patient does not. A framing in which manganism is simply reversible on removal does not fit the reported courses, and the entry avoids it.

selected_evidence.snippet: The neurologic deficits did not resolve after patients discontinued methcathinone use.
